analyst_view.overall: United are 17th with seven points and one league win in nine. Michael Carrick is under heavy pressure, although Wednesday's 3-2 Champions League comeback against Roma bought him some time. Villa are unbeaten in five league games but lost 3-0 at Barcelona in midweek, and Unai Emery is reportedly close to a new contract. United are without Lisandro Martinez (suspended), Shaw, Ugarte, Baleba and Sesko. Villa are missing Matty Cash (suspended), Onana and Ruggeri, and Wan-Bissaka needs a late fitness test.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. United are one of only two sides without a league clean sheet and have conceded 15, and they have no natural left-back with Shaw out and Dorgu doubtful. Villa have made seven errors leading to goals this season, the joint-most in the league, and Nicolas Jackson has five league goals. Both defences look shaky, so we lean higher.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. United should have more of the ball at home while Villa counter, and that matches the model, so we stay with it.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards, already high. Chris Kavanagh referees a high-pressure game, and both teams have recent suspensions (Martinez was sent off against Chelsea, and Cash reached five yellows). That supports the high figure rather than pushing it further up.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots, with 17.4 for United. United have scored only five league goals in their last six and are without striker Sesko, while Rashford is a doubt. Their high home total looks optimistic, so we lean slightly lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. United's weaker attack is balanced by two error-prone defences, so we stay close to the model.
